name: HandsOn Triangle
description: A Triangle-area volunteer opportunity database where students can browse roles by date, interest, organization, and community need, making it easier to find meaningful ways to get involved locally.

name: Student Action Board
description: A leadership-focused service program where students identify local needs, plan service projects, and build teamwork and community impact skills.

name: Habitat for Humanity of Durham
description: Volunteer opportunities supporting affordable housing projects in Durham, including build days, site support, and community-based events.

name: Teen Board Sponsored Habitat for Humanity of Durham
description: A teen leadership group (roughly ages 14–18) that supports youth builds, mentoring, advocacy, and community engagement projects.

name: SEEDs Volunteering
description: Volunteer with SEEDs by submitting the volunteer form to help with community garden and environmental projects.

name: Church World Service (CWS) Durham
description: Volunteer with refugee and immigrant support efforts through direct services, advocacy, and community connection programs in Durham.

name: Communities Acting for Refugee Empowerment (CARE)
description: A community support program that pairs refugee individuals and families with local groups that help with education, goals, and long-term stability.

name: Environmental Educations of North Carolina
description: The Environmental Educators of North Carolina (EENC) offers volunteer opportunities through committees, action projects, and special events. Volunteering allows educators to support the statewide community, share their voice, and connect with fellow professionals.

name: Durham Arts Summer Arts Teen Volunteer Program
description: Summer Arts Camps offer rising 10th–12th grade students the chance to volunteer alongside instructors, support staff, and create art with younger campers. The program provides hands-on experience, builds resumes, and can count toward school or organization volunteer requirements.

name: Hub Farm Volunteer Opportunities
description: Hub Farm offers a variety of volunteer opportunities, from working with animals and the land to supporting fundraising efforts. Individuals, families, and groups are welcome to get involved and make a hands-on impact.

name: Food Bank of Central & Eastern North Carolina
description: Create meaningful change in just one shift by sorting and packing food, supporting community distributions, and helping neighbors in need. Every hour you volunteer moves us closer to a future without hunger.

name: Meals on Wheels Durham
description: Meals on Wheels Durham depends on dedicated volunteers to help deliver meals to seniors, individuals with disabilities, and homebound adults who cannot prepare food on their own. With morning volunteer opportunities available Monday through Friday, you’ll see firsthand how a nutritious meal, a friendly smile, and a kind word can make a meaningful difference.

name: Urban Ministries of Durham
description: Urban Ministries of Durham works with the community to combat homelessness and poverty by providing food, shelter, and pathways to a better future for neighbors in need.

name: Inter-Faith FOOD Shuttle
description: We offer a variety of meaningful group and individual volunteer opportunities, including preparing and packing meals, delivering BackPack Buddies, assisting with food recovery, building raised-bed garden boxes, and helping with farm projects—each making a direct impact in the community.

name: InStepp Volunteering Opportunities
description: You can get involved as an InStepp Ambassador by applying through the Volunteer Application Form at volunteer@instepp.org. Opportunities include Communications Volunteers, who help with writing, social media, or newsletters, and Short-Term Project Volunteers for one-time projects with flexible time commitments.

name: Boys & Girls Clubs of Durham and Orange Counties
description: Volunteers are vital to delivering BGCDOC programs and services that support Durham and Chapel Hill youth. By giving your time as a program or event volunteer, you can make a lasting difference in the lives and futures of our members.

name: Kramden Institute Volunteering
description: Kramden is a community-driven organization powered by the dedication of volunteers who share their time and passion. From refurbishing computers and distributing them to students to supporting recycling drives, volunteers play a vital role in advancing Kramden’s mission.

name: Durham Food Pantry
description: End Hunger Durham is seeking volunteers with IT, graphics, and fundraising skills. Volunteers can help manage the organization’s WordPress website, post newsletters through Mailchimp, assist with occasional digital tools like SurveyMonkey or Evite, design flyers and brochures, and support fundraising efforts such as grants, events, and donor outreach. If you are interested in helping fight food insecurity in our community, please contact endhungerd@gmail.com

name: End Hunger Steering Community
description: If you believe that food is a human right and are interested in working with a community-based organization that collaborates with people experiencing hunger as well as decision-makers who shape related policies, consider joining the End Hunger Durham Steering Committee. Committee members help guide priorities, plan events, support fundraising efforts, and contribute to key program work. If you are interested, contact Jacquelyn Blackwell at endhungerd@gmail.com.

name: Porch Durham
description: The PORCH for Schools program partners with Durham schools to support students from preschool through high school who experience food insecurity. By working closely with school staff and parent coordinators, the program provides customized monthly food distributions—including family food bags, choice pantries, afterschool snacks, and summer meals—as well as grocery gift cards during school breaks to help families meet their needs when students are home.

name: Durham Earth Day Festival Volunteer
description: Interested in volunteering for the Earth Day celebration? Visit our iVolunteer site to sign up. Volunteers will receive an Earth Day festival T-shirt, along with snacks and water during the event.

name: Bimbé Cultural Arts Festival Volunteer
description: Interested in volunteering at the Bimbé Cultural Arts Festival? Sign up through our iVolunteer site to help support this exciting community celebration. Volunteers will assist with event activities and help make the festival a great experience for everyone attending.

name: Annual Egg Hunt at West Point on the Eno Volunteer
description: Volunteer Egg Hunters Wanted! Join us for the Annual Egg Hunt at West Point on the Eno and help make this event a fun and memorable experience for children ages 0–12. Volunteers (ages 14 and up) will assist with the egg hunt beginning at 10:15 a.m., including the search for the special golden egg, and help with games and crafts afterward while supporting this long-standing community tradition.

name: Durham Senior Games Volunteer
description: It’s time again for the Durham Senior Games, and volunteers are needed to help make this exciting event run smoothly. The games rely on the teamwork and dedication of staff and volunteers to create a joyful and rewarding experience for participants. If you have availability, please consider signing up to support this year’s events and help celebrate the achievements of our senior community.

name: Astronomy Lovers Wanted! Volunteer Under the Stars
description: Durham Parks and Recreation is seeking enthusiastic volunteers to help make the Silver Screen & Starry Skies event a memorable evening for the community. This unique outdoor program combines a movie night with hands-on astronomy activities, including moon viewing and stargazing, followed by a screening of the classic space film Apollo 13. Volunteers will assist with event setup and breakdown, guest check-in, activity support, and general event assistance while helping create a welcoming atmosphere for guests of all ages. The event is weather-dependent, with a backup date planned if needed.

name: Volunteer Opportunity: Ties and Tiaras! Mardi Gras
description: Help create a magical evening for families in the community by volunteering at Ties and Tiaras: Mardi Gras, hosted by Durham Parks and Recreation. This festive event invites parents and children to dress up and enjoy a night of dancing, dinner, dessert, and Mardi Gras–themed fun. Volunteers will help support the event and ensure families have a welcoming and memorable experience at the Durham Armory.

name: Invasive Plant Removal at West Point on the Eno
description: Join Durham Parks and Recreation and the Eno River Association for a volunteer stewardship day at West Point on the Eno. Volunteers will help remove invasive plants and support conservation efforts alongside outdoor recreation staff, helping protect this treasured natural space. Participants must be 16 or older, and no experience is necessary—tools and gloves will be provided, and volunteers are encouraged to wear sturdy clothing suitable for outdoor work.

name: Youth Volunteer Corps of the Greater Triangle
description: Youth Volunteer Corps of the Greater Triangle (YVC) invites youth ages 11–18 to participate in monthly service projects that support a variety of community causes. Participants develop leadership skills, make a meaningful impact in their community, and earn service hours for school clubs and college applications.

name: Park and Trail Volunteer Service Projects
description: Community volunteers can propose and carry out service and improvement projects to enhance parks and trails through an application process with Durham Parks and Recreation. Past volunteer projects have included removing invasive species, planting trees and flower beds, building kiosks and footbridges, and installing litter traps in waterways.

name: Briggs Avenue Community Garden
description: Briggs Avenue Community Garden is a forested community space in East Durham dedicated to helping families grow healthy food, learn about sustainable agriculture, support pollinators, and strengthen local food security. The garden offers free, hands-on agricultural education and welcomes people of all ages in a supportive environment focused on community building and access to growing resources.

name: Durham County Extension Master Food Volunteer Program
description: The Extension Master Food Volunteer (EMFV) program is designed for individuals who want to support their community through food-related activities. Participants share their interest in cooking, nutrition, and food education while helping others learn about healthy eating and the value of connecting through meals.

name: Welcome Baby
description: Volunteers help make our work possible by supporting parenting workshops and safety classes, assisting with the Giving Closet, and helping host community events that connect parents, educators, and supporters. They also provide valuable office and outreach support that keeps programs running smoothly, making a meaningful difference whether they volunteer occasionally or on a regular basis.

name: Durham County Library Volunteer
description: Durham County Library Volunteers support library staff by helping with a variety of tasks that enhance programs and services for the community. Volunteers may assist with organizing materials, supporting library events and activities, helping with youth programs, and contributing to a welcoming environment for visitors.

name: Dix Park Volunteer
description: Thank you for your interest in volunteering with Raleigh Parks! To sign up for an upcoming event, select the event button to view the details, then click the register button at the bottom of the listing. If you’d like step-by-step guidance, you can also watch a video demonstration.

name: Cary Teen Council
description: The Cary Teen Council is a volunteer organization made up of teens from schools across Cary and surrounding areas that promotes leadership, accountability, and service. Members gain experience through volunteer work, leadership opportunities, and participation in programs focused on community service, education, teamwork, fundraising, and event planning while building strong communication and time management skills.

name: WakeMed Junior Volunteer Program
description: For students interested in healthcare, the WakeMed Summer Teen Volunteer Program offers a structured clinical volunteering experience at the Raleigh Campus or Cary Hospital. Participants are placed in specific departments where they assist staff and interact with patients and visitors, gaining real insight into the medical field while contributing to the local community, with the option to continue after completing 30 hours of service.

name: Sierra Club - Environmental Volunteering
description: The Sierra Club offers students the opportunity to engage in grassroots environmental activism through local and national efforts focused on conservation, clean air and water, and climate action. With chapters across all 50 states, it is ideal for students looking to make an impact in environmental advocacy and sustainability.

name: Youth Conservation Crews - Conservation Corps North Carolina
description: Youth Conservation Crews, part of Conservation Corps North Carolina, offers teens ages 15–18 hands-on summer experiences in conservation through projects like trail building, habitat restoration, and forestry. With both day and camping options, it is ideal for students interested in environmental service, outdoor work, and sustainability.
